subject: Token smoothing & package structure — proposal and sample math
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Token smoothing & packaging question

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the intro last week. We're finalizing vendor comparisons and I have a couple of specific questions about how Redwood would meter and bill our use case: long product-descriptions + multi-turn chat history for support (average prompt input ~1.2k tokens, responses ~400 tokens).

Two things we need clarity on before RFP scoring:
- How you apply the minimum/billing quantum for short bursts vs sustained sessions (do you ceil per call or aggregate across session windows?)
- Whether you offer a smoothing/rounding policy for hybrid pipelines (embedding + generation) so that we don't get penalized by microbursts from search indexing jobs.

If you have a short example invoice or sample calculations, that would be super helpful. Also: tentative timeline is procurement review by Oct 25.

Best,
Alex
Procurement Lead, BrightRetail

Attachment: none
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Token smoothing & packaging question

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: we support both per-call and session-aggregated billing models and can propose a smoothing pilot to reduce microburst volatility. Below is a concise summary and I attached a short pricing_v1.pdf with examples.

Summary options (high level):
1) Per-call (ceil to 1 token quantum = 10 tokens) — simplest, predictable for spikes.
2) Session-aggregation (30-minute sliding window) — we aggregate calls for a session ID and bill on the aggregated token sum, then apply quantum rounding once. Good for chat-heavy UX.
3) Hybrid smoothing pilot — baseline per-call billing but we credit ephemeral bursts coming from indexing pipelines up to an agreed monthly cap.

Proposal ask: can you share a small sample of daily call volume for the indexing pipeline vs chat? I can run a quick example calculation and follow up with a short proposal PDF + CSV showing line-item math.

Next steps: quick 20-min call tomorrow morning to align on volumes? Camila will join for the technical details.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Priya / Markus — quick internal note ahead of the call. Alex is asking for smoothing and a pilot discount. A few points to consider for the proposal:
- We should propose a pilot with a modest uplift to minimum (to preserve unit economics) but with a smoothing credit for microburst indexing up to X tokens/month.
- Suggested discount structure: 10% off list above $10k MRC, tiered to 18% above $50k. For pilot, consider an additional 5% one-time concession to close deciders.
- Need ops approval for session-aggregation window (30min vs 60min) — 30min preferred to avoid cross-user mixing.

I can model example invoice lines if you want me to produce a CSV (samples: avg-chat-1.6k tokens/session, indexing bursts ~50k tokens/day but heavy bursty).

Ben

Thanks Ben — agree with the pilot and the concession. A couple of firm asks before we send to procurement:
- Offer a 30-day smoothing pilot: aggregate per-session for billing and refund any monthly overage above the rolling median of indexing bursts for the pilot duration.
- Keep the token quantum at 10 tokens for rounding, but for the pilot allow one rounding pass per session window (reduces rounding noise).
- Approve a one-time 5% pilot concession subject to renewal terms locked in the contract (auto-revert to standard tiering if no renewal).

Priya: please draft the proposal PDF and include a worked example CSV showing three invoice scenarios (baseline, pilot with smoothing, pilot with smoothing + concession). We'll review before sending.

-Markus
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>, BrightRetail Finance <finance@brightretail.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood proposal: token smoothing pilot + sample invoice math (BR-2026-024)

Alex — thanks for the call earlier this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a short proposal and a CSV with line-item math. Key points up front:

- Pilot mechanics (30 days):
  • Session-aggregation window: 30 minutes. All calls tagged with a session_id are summed within the window and rounded once to the 10-token quantum.
  • Microburst smoothing credit: Redwood will credit indexing-origin tokens above the rolling median daily burst up to 1.5M tokens during the pilot period. Excess is billed at standard rates.
  • Quantum & rounding: tokens are bucketed in 10-token quanta; rounding performed at the aggregation step for session-aggregation calls.

- Commercials:
  • MRC: $9,500 (list) with pilot concession: 5% off MRC during pilot = $9,025/month.
  • Usage tiers post-pilot: 10% discount above $10k, 18% above $50k (standard contract mapping).
  • Sample invoice (see CSV): shows baseline (no smoothing), pilot-smoothed, and pilot-smoothed + concession. Example: for a month with 3.2M tokens from chat + 1.8M tokens indexing (heavy bursts), pilot-smoothed invoice reduces billable tokens by ~12% vs baseline due to session aggregation + smoothing credits.

- Next steps:
  1) Sign off on pilot mechanics & cap (confirm 1.5M smoothing cap).
  2) Procurement: we'll produce a short SOW and add the pilot concession clause.
  3) Ops: Camila will schedule onboarding and add instrumentation tags for indexing traffic.

I've attached redwood_proposal_BR-2026-024.pdf and token_smoothing_example.csv with the worked examples. If procurement wants, we can map invoice line items to a PO-friendly layout.

Would you like the SOW draft by end of week?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0126
